papers.title_in_file: Matrix Product State on a Quantum Computer
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, results and conclusion read; appendices and reference lists skimmed or not read.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a quantum matrix product state (qMPS) and a variational DMRG-style method for ground-state search, tested in numerical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that in numerical simulations of variational quantum singular value decomposition on random states, all simulated results reach a fidelity exceeding 96%, with fidelities above 99% for systems involving up to 7 qubits.
quotes: All simulated results reach a fidelity exceeding 96%, with fidelities above 99% for systems involving up to 7 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation on random states, one study.

assertions.value: The authors report from numerical simulation of Heisenberg spin-chain Hamiltonians that vqMPS reaches accuracy comparable to full-scale VQE, with each local VQE optimization involving at most 3 qubits.
quotes: For all the cases, we find the vqMPS can reach a comparable accuracy compared with VQE when using merely
each local optimization by VQE involves at most 3 qubits.

assertions.value: The authors state that the VQE comparison ran 300 iterations, that circuit depth and iteration count were limited, and that the optimization may therefore not reach the ground truth.
quotes: We performed 300 iterations and reached a good convergence for each optimization process.
Since the depth of the circuits as well as the number of iterations are limited, the optimization process may not reach the ground truth.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own simulation setup, Sec. V, p.8.

assertions.value: The authors state that the result is strongly correlated with the quality of the optimization, including the QSVD and VQE procedures, and that accuracy can be further improved using deterministic algorithms on error-corrected devices.
quotes: However, the result is strongly correlated with the quality of the optimization, including the procedures of QSVD and the VQE.
The accuracy of vqMPS can be further improved using deterministic algorithms on quantum devices with error corrections.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit in the Conclusion, p.8.

papers.title_in_file: Practical Quantum Reservoir Computing in Rydberg Atom Arrays
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, results and conclusion read; appendices and reference lists skimmed or not read.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical comparison of single-step and multi-step quantum reservoir computing on a simulated Rydberg atom array under sampling noise and decoherence.

assertions.value: The authors report from numerical simulation that sampling noise drastically reduces the information processing capacity of multi-step QRC, while single-step QRC keeps its capacity up to the third order under finite shots.
assertions.anchor: Sec. IV, Fig. 5, text on time-series tasks
quotes: sampling noise drastically reduces its capacity.
its IPC maintains up to the third order under finite Ns
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors report that single-step QRC reaches 100% classification accuracy in the asymptotic limit of infinite shots, and that with finite shots accuracy stays over 98% using the derandomized classical shadow protocol.
quotes: the SS-QRC achieves 100% classification accuracy.
the classification accuracy maintains over 98% for the derandomized classical shadow protocol
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated classification result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work is a comparative numerical study of single-step and multi-step QRC architectures implemented on a Rydberg atom array.
quotes: Here, we provide a comparative numerical study of single-step-QRC (SS-QRC) and multi-step-QRC (MS-QRC) architectures implemented on a Rydberg atom array.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own scope in the Abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: No experiment on hardware is reported in the quoted scope statement.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum reservoir computing in atomic lattices
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, results and conclusion read; appendices and reference lists skimmed or not read.
papers.what_it_is: Numerical study of quantum reservoir computing on a one-dimensional Bose-Hubbard lattice with homogeneous couplings.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in the one-dimensional Bose-Hubbard reservoir with homogeneous couplings, performance on different tasks can be enhanced either in the chaotic regime or in the weak interaction limit.
quotes: we find that performance in different tasks can be enhanced either in the chaotic regime or in the weak interaction limit.

assertions.value: The authors report that the one-dimensional chain with open boundaries consistently outperformed other topologies across various benchmarks.
quotes: The one-dimensional chain with open boundaries consistently outperformed other topologies across various benchmarks.

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains to be tested whether their conclusions hold in larger reservoirs.
quotes: It will be interesting to test the validity of these conclusions in larger reservoirs.

papers.title_in_file: Unsupervised Feature Extraction and Reconstruction Using Parameterized Quantum Circuits
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, results and conclusion read; appendices and reference lists skimmed or not read.
papers.what_it_is: Evaluates a quantum autoencoder with QCNN and other encoders for MNIST feature extraction and reconstruction, in simulation and on IonQ.

assertions.value: The authors report that with a QCNN-based encoder the quantum autoencoder reaches an average accuracy of 97.59% in binary classification of MNIST (0 and 1), against 88.40 % and 88.78 % for two other architectures.
quotes: with a QCNN-based encoder, QAE achieves an average accuracy of 97.59% in binary classification of MNIST (0 and 1)
significantly outperforming architectures A and B, which achieved 88.40 % and 88.78 %, respectively.

assertions.value: The authors report that the quantum autoencoder's reconstruction results are relatively underwhelming, and that they identify limitations in its reconstruction capability.
quotes: its reconstruction results are relatively underwhelming.

assertions.value: The authors report that performance on 3-class and 4-class classifications was not very satisfactory, and that on the IonQ quantum computer with 100 MNIST data points and 1000 shots the performance fell short of expectations.
quotes: the QAE's performance on 3-class and 4-class classifications was not very satisfactory.
we tested 100 MNIST data points (50 zeros and 50 ones) on the IonQ quantum computer using 1000 shots.

assertions.value: The authors state that accuracy was computed on 400 randomly selected test samples, with training simulation using 8 qubits compressed to 1 qubit.
quotes: We randomly selected 400 samples from the test dataset to calculate accuracy.
Training simulation using 8 qubits and compressed to 1 qubit
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in Sec. VII.B.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Optimization Workflows for the Shipment Selection Problem
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, results and conclusion read; appendices and reference lists skimmed or not read.
papers.what_it_is: IonQ and Einride hybrid workflow using Iterative-QAOA as a warm start for a classical vehicle routing solver on a shipment selection problem.

assertions.value: The authors report that when the quantum-derived solution is passed to the classical solver as a warm start, plans achieve a mean SD improvement of +1.7% and a mean reduction of 0.2% in drive distance per shipment across all weekly schedules and scenarios, while total operational cost remains effectively unchanged.
quotes: the resulting QWS plans achieve a mean SD improvement of +1.7% and a mean reduction of 0.2% in drive distance per shipment across all weekly schedules and scenarios
assertions.certainty_reason: Results from one study by the vendor's own authors.
assertions.reader_inference: Authors are IonQ employees; the baseline is Einride's EOS solver, not an independent classical optimum.

assertions.value: The authors report improvements of up to 12% in SD and a reduction of up to 6% in total drive distance per shipment for specific instances.
quotes: achieves improvements of up to 12% in SD and a reduction of up to 6% in total drive distance per shipment for specific instances
assertions.certainty_reason: Best-case instance results from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the subset of instances within reach of current devices, the workflow was also executed on IonQ trapped-ion quantum hardware, where the hardware results closely reproduce the noiseless simulations.
quotes: the workflow is additionally executed on IonQ trapped-ion quantum hardware, where the hardware results closely reproduce the noiseless simulations
assertions.certainty_reason: Hardware run reported by the vendor.

assertions.value: The authors state that the evaluation spans up to 130 qubits and that the large-instance simulations rely on MPS approximations with fixed bond dimension, so part of the performance loss on the largest instances may reflect tensor network truncation.
quotes: enabling evaluation on real, anonymized logistics data spanning up to 130 qubits.
Third, the present large-instance simulations rely on MPS approximations with fixed bond dimension, so part of the performance loss on the largest instances may reflect tensor network truncation
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in Sec. V Conclusions and Outlook.

papers.title_in_file: Qlustering for Data Clustering via Network-Based Quantum Transport
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, results and conclusion read; appendices and reference lists skimmed or not read.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes Qlustering, unsupervised clustering from steady-state output currents of a quantum transport network, simulated and compared with k-means.

assertions.value: The authors report that on synthetic point clusters Qlustering achieved perfect clustering (RI = ARI = 1) for small group widths, with performance reduced as the width increases.
quotes: For small widths, Qlustering achieved perfect clustering (RI = ARI = 1), while increasing the width reduced performance.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work is a theoretical proof of concept and that they do not attempt an exhaustive benchmark against the full landscape of clustering algorithms, using k-means as the reference method.
quotes: Since the present work is intended as a theoretical proof of concept, we do not attempt an exhaustive benchmark against the full landscape of clustering algorithms.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Iris dataset with all four features included, k-means outperforms Qlustering on most metrics, and state that Qlustering may struggle with convex or linearly separable data structures under certain configurations.
quotes: With all four features included, k-means outperforms Qlustering on most metrics.
This suggests that Qlustering may struggle with convex or linearly separable data structures under certain configurations.

papers.title_in_file: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning Advantages with Noises
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, results and conclusion read; appendices and reference lists skimmed or not read.
papers.what_it_is: Theory paper giving a classical error-rectification algorithm for quantum Fourier sampling and proofs for noisy agnostic parity learning and its classical verification.

assertions.value: The authors prove that their classical error-rectification algorithm can restore the heavy Fourier coefficients using a small number of noisy samples that scales logarithmically with the problem size.
quotes: we prove that the error-rectification algorithm can restore the heavy Fourier coefficients by using a small number of noisy samples that scales logarithmically with the problem size.

assertions.value: The authors prove that agnostic parity learning with uniform input marginal can be accomplished efficiently on noisy quantum devices with their algorithm, with sample, time and space complexities scaling at most polynomially with system size.
quotes: prove that this task can be accomplished in an efficient way on noisy quantum devices with our algorithm.
the sample, time, and space complexities scale at most polynomially with the system size, for both classical and quantum computers.

assertions.value: The authors prove that a classical client with access to the random example oracle can efficiently verify the agnostic parity learning results from the noisy quantum prover, under the condition that the Fourier coefficients are sparse.
quotes: we prove that a classical client with access to the random example oracle can verify the agnostic parity learning results from the noisy quantum prover in an efficient way, under the condition that the Fourier coefficients are sparse.

assertions.value: The authors state that Theorem 1 requires bit flip errors to occur randomly and independently for each qubit, a condition they say can be relaxed if the error strength stays below a constant threshold.
quotes: Theorem 1 requires that bit flip errors occur randomly and independently for each qubit.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated after Theorem 1 in the main text.

papers.title_in_file: Classical and Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning for Trigger-Like Event Selection on CMS Open Data
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, results and conclusion read; appendices and reference lists skimmed or not read.
papers.what_it_is: An eight-qubit, PCA-constrained benchmark of four classical and four hybrid quantum models on a CMS open-data trigger-like classification task, in state-vector simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that the strongest classical model, an artificial neural network, reached 93.53 percent accuracy and 0.9819 ROC-AUC, and the strongest quantum model, a quantum convolutional network, reached 90.89 percent accuracy and 0.9731 ROC-AUC.
quotes: The strongest classical model is the artificial neural network, at 93.53 percent accuracy and 0.9819 ROC-AUC
The quantum convolutional network is the strongest, at 90.89 percent accuracy and 0.9731 ROC-AUC

assertions.value: The authors state that the study shows parity rather than advantage for quantum models in this regime, and is meant as a controlled reference point rather than a claim of quantum advantage.
quotes: Read honestly, the study shows parity rather than advantage for quantum models in this regime
The study is meant as a controlled reference point rather than a claim of quantum advantage.
assertions.reader_inference: The classical models used more input features than the quantum models, so the comparison is not resource-matched (see limitation assertions).

assertions.value: The authors state that because the label is defined on invariant mass and the inputs are the four-vector components used to compute it, the models are in large part reconstructing a known analytic function from its own ingredients, so a high area under the curve is expected.
quotes: the models are in large part reconstructing a known analytic function from its own ingredients.

assertions.value: The authors state that the classical models use the full feature set while the quantum models use sixteen principal components, and that results come from a single split and a single seed without error bars, cross-validation or repeated runs.
quotes: The classical models use the full feature set, while the quantum models use sixteen principal components
The results come from a single split and a single seed, without error bars, cross-validation or repeated runs
